name: Launch Post-Sale Purchase — Access + Welcome, Promo Stop, Next Follow-Up

source.spec: launch-automations.spec.md §3.3 — Post-sale purchase: Paid (main / each upsell / each downsell) → access + welcome, stop promotional emails, start next follow-up
source.capability_note: automation-templates/launch-ghl-probe/GHL-CAPABILITY-NOTE.md — post-sale purchase: Skill 44 engine; Order Submitted / Payment received trigger is not auto-built; engine + patch-trigger/browser; workflow_goal is a VERIFIED_ACTION
source.purchase_spec: Signature_Launch_Muse_Specifications/14_SKILL_44_PURCHASE_AUTOMATIONS_SPEC.md §6–§7 — short purchase handler, no long waits, buyer suppression, entitlement once per line

purpose: One short purchase handler per paid point. It fires on a verified paid transaction line, grants the matching access and welcome, stops every promotional email and text for that buyer immediately, then starts that buyer's next follow-up. It never waits, never sends a promo, and never requires a thank-you page visit to grant access.

trigger.primary_event: Order line paid — payment verified as settled (not merely order submitted)
trigger.trigger_build: Not created by CampaignBuilder (Tag Added only). Build with `caf workflows patch-trigger --trigger-json <file>` on the internal API, snapshot before write; Tier-4 managed browser where the engine has no verified payload.

variants.match: Approved launch-plan binding for the main offer: product ID + price ID + order-page/form ID. Never inferred from a human-readable product name.
variants.next_follow_up: Main upsell follow-up when an upsell page exists; otherwise onboarding / review sequence.

variants.match: One variant per upsell page: that page's product ID + price ID + order-page/form ID from the approved launch plan.
variants.next_follow_up: The next upsell in the stack, the matching downsell after a decline, or onboarding when the stack ends.

variants.match: One variant per downsell page: that page's product ID + price ID + order-page/form ID from the approved launch plan.
variants.next_follow_up: The next downsell in the stack, or onboarding when the stack ends.

entry_conditions: A verified paid transaction line exists for this tenant and contact
The line resolves to exactly one approved variant binding (main, upsell N, or downsell N)
Entitlement + campaign version recorded for idempotent action keys
exit_conditions: Access and welcome delivered once for this transaction line
Buyer removed from all promotional sends for this launch
Buyer enrolled in exactly one next follow-up
trigger.reentry: Deliberate per transaction line. A later distinct upsell/downsell purchase may enter again; the same transaction line must not repeat access, welcome, suppression or enrollment. Dedupe on tenant + verified transaction/order-line identity + action type + campaign version — never on contact ID alone, order ID alone, or 'has tag'.

channels: SMS (only when the launch plan has email + text and A2P is approved)

sequence.name: Stop promotional sends first
sequence.timing: Immediately — before welcome or next follow-up
sequence.detail: Remove every launch promotional tag on the buyer and set the buyer-suppressed state. Remove from promotional campaigns and from abandoned-checkout / recovery workflows. A queued promo must be suppressed before it sends; suppression is the first action, not a later one.

sequence.name: Mark buyer + variant
sequence.detail: Add the launch buyer tag and the variant tag (main / upsell-N / downsell-N) used by reporting and by the next follow-up. Tags carry the approved variant, never a guessed product name.

sequence.name: Access + welcome email
sequence.detail: Deliver the access link for the exact purchased variant, the receipt reference, and the next step. Copy comes from the approved Skill 50 welcome/access sequence; this template wires it and does not author it.

sequence.name: Access + welcome text
sequence.timing: Immediately (when email + text launch and A2P approved)
sequence.detail: Short access link and reply invitation with STOP opt-out and the launch send window. Skipped entirely when A2P is not approved; the build plan records the skip.

sequence.name: Start the next follow-up
sequence.detail: Enroll in exactly one variant-appropriate next follow-up (next upsell, downsell after a decline, or onboarding at the end of the stack). Never enroll the buyer in the promotional launch sequence.

sequence.name: Close the handler
sequence.detail: Goal/exit node ends the short handler. No nurture waits live here; longer onboarding and review sequences are separate workflows.

buyer_suppression.rule: A paid buyer receives no further promotional emails or texts for this launch, for any variant.
stops: Remaining upsell/downsell pitches for an offer already bought or included in the package
does_not_stop: The buyer's own onboarding / review / referral sequence
A genuinely different later offer approved in the launch plan

build.engine: Skill 44 internal-API engine (`caf workflows create` / `CampaignBuilder`), with the managed-browser Tier-4 backstop for the trigger and any unverified payload
build.api_ceiling: The official GHL API has no workflow create, update, publish or trigger endpoint; its only workflow operation is GET /workflows/. Do not attempt an API-only build.
build.state: Every workflow is created as a draft. Triggers are written `status: draft`; nothing goes live. Live switch-on is a separate client approval.
inputs_required: Approved variant bindings: product ID, price ID, order-page/form ID per main / upsell / downsell
Location whitelist entry and Firebase refresh token (workflow writes); absent token → Tier-4 browser backstop

quality.wf_checks: WF-1..21 and FAB-QC >= 8.5 apply to the built workflow
assertions: Suppression runs before any welcome or follow-up step
No wait step longer than the short handler allows
Access granted once per verified transaction line
No promo node remains reachable for a paid buyer
Everything is draft_only; no live switch-on
No client account touched during the build
